text.tspan: In-car race telemetry module: PIC18F57Q84 + BG95-M3 Mini PCIe (UDP uplink / downlink) + NEO-M9N GNSS
Sheet 0 is the system overview and the cross-board net list. Sheets A-D are the four detail schematics, unchanged, each generated from its own script and matching its own BOM 1:1.
(0) SYSTEM OVERVIEW - every inter-block connection. Pin numbers: U1 = 48-pin TQFP, J2 = 52-pin Mini PCIe edge, U4 = 24-pin LCC. Wires that cross WITHOUT a dot are not connected.
no PWRKEY: boots with its rail
FB2, DCR < 0.2 ohm | VCC ramp must land in 66 us - 26.4 ms
CROSS-BOARD NET LIST - every signal crossing a block boundary. No level shifters anywhere: the card's UART and control pins are 3.3 V, and the NEO shares the PIC's rail.
U1 <-> J2 BG95-M3 Mini PCIe socket
Card-relative names, ALREADY CROSSED: pin 11 is "connect to
the DTE's TX". Do not cross the pair a second time.
No hardware flow control exists on the NEO-M9N. TIMEPULSE is
routed even though the firmware does not use it yet: hardware
capture beats UART arrival time by orders of magnitude for
tying a position fix to lap timing.
U1 <-> U5 / J_icsp console and programming
U5 TXD already drives the PIC RX - do not cross again.
Programming and in-circuit debug are J_icsp with a PICkit 5;
the PIC18F57Q84 has no USB peripheral, so USB-C is console only.
RAILS. VBAT_IN 7-18 V -> VSYS -> two independent bucks. 3V3_CELL absorbs the BG95's 2.7 A 2G bursts; 3V3_SYS stays quiet for the PIC, the NEO-M9N and the USB bridge, so a transmit
burst cannot brown out the MCU or the GNSS receiver. Both rails are 3.3 V and must stay 3.3 V - raising either one breaks cross-rail logic levels. Single ground plane throughout.
BOOT ORDER. Buck B is always enabled, so the PIC and the NEO-M9N come up together and can never drive each other while one is unpowered. Buck A's EN pull-down holds the modem off while
the PIC is in reset; the PIC then drives CELL_PWR_EN high and the card auto-powers on - there is no PWRKEY on this card. PERST# is for recovering a wedged modem, not for boot.
READING SHEETS A-D. Within them, connections are made by NET-LABEL TAG rather than by long wires, and the same tag name on two tiles is the same net: 3V3_SYS on sheet A is the same copper
as 3V3_SYS on sheets B and D. Reference designators only are printed; component values live in the matching BOM markdown. Pin budget and PPS checks: interconnect-and-pin-budget.md.
Reference designators shown; component values are in power-supply-bom.md
(2) BUCK A U2 TPS54560-Q1 : VSYS -> 3.3 V (>=4 A, 2G-capable) -> 3V3_CELL
(3) BUCK B U3 LMR16006X : VSYS -> 3.3 V (~0.6 A) -> 3V3_SYS (comp + soft-start internal)
EN floats = ON. Optional R_enB 100k -> VSYS,
or a divider to set a custom UVLO.
Card is self-contained: on-card VBAT regulation, RF/BB decoupling + ferrite are INSIDE the module.
The raw-module VBAT star network (ferrite + MLCC arrays + 2x TVS) is NOT built on our board.
(A) POWER RAILS component values in power-supply-bom.md
FARSEER MCU SUPPORT CIRCUIT - PIC18F57Q84, 48-pin TQFP
Every resistor and capacitor shows its VALUE next to the reference designator. MPN / status / cost: mcu-bom.md
All pin numbers are the 48-pin TQFP column (DS40002213F Figure 2-7 / Table 3-2)
to buck A EN - HIGH = rail on
to J_icsp pin 5 - keep clear of everything else
to J_icsp pin 4 - keep clear of everything else
status LED, drives low to light
No AVDD / AVSS and no VCAP on this device, so ADC quality depends entirely on how clean 3V3_SYS is at
pins 7 and 30 - there is no analog supply to filter separately, and VREF is not a dedicated pin (it would
cost RA2 / RA3). Unused I/O: drive low in firmware (DS40002213F 4.6) or tie to VSS through 1-10 kOhm.
(2) SUPPLY AND DECOUPLING : 0.1 uF per VDD pin, REQUIRED (DS40002213F 4.2.1)
Pins 7/6 and 30/31 sit on OPPOSITE CORNERS of the package, so these are two genuinely separate placements -
one shared cap is not compliant. Each cap: ceramic, self-resonant at 200 MHz or above, same side of the board
as the MCU, trace no longer than 6 mm, and power routed to the CAP FIRST and then on to the device pin.
Lift C_mclr here if the programmer objects to the RC (Figure 4-2).
A no-fit pad on C_mclr does the same job for free.
All three parts within 6 mm of pin 20 (4.3). R_mclr1 <= 10 kOhm and R_mclr2 <= 470 Ohm are datasheet limits,
not suggestions: R_mclr2 caps the current C_mclr can dump into MCLR during an ESD/EOS breakdown. The Curiosity
Nano fits 47 kOhm and no capacitor, which violates R1 <= 10 kOhm - follow the datasheet, not the dev board.
(4) ICSP PROGRAM + DEBUG HEADER - PICkit 5 (Microchip PICkit pinout, Figures 48-1 / 48-2)
SENSE ONLY - leave "Power target circuit from tool" OFF in MPLAB.
The board runs the NEO-M9N, two bucks and a 2.7 A BG95 card; the
PICkit cannot supply it, and reports a target-voltage error if asked.
DS40002213F 4.4 is emphatic about what NOT to add: no pull-UPS, series diodes, or capacitors on ICSPCLK /
ICSPDAT - they interfere with programmer communications. R_icsp1/2 are ESD series only and must not exceed
100 Ohm; the 47 kOhm pull-DOWNS are what Microchip debug tooling expects. Nothing else may share RB6 / RB7.
THIS HEADER IS BOTH PROGRAMMER AND DEBUGGER, permanently, not a manufacturing fixture. The device offers
In-Circuit Debug with three breakpoints over the SAME two pins (DS40002213F p. 6); MPLAB clears DEBUG
(CONFIG7[5]) for a debug session and no board change is needed. JTAG is not an alternative - 39 states the
PIC18-Q84 JTAG module does not support programming. Leave LVP (CONFIG4[5]) at its erased 1: clearing it
forces high-voltage VPP entry from then on, and only HV programming can ever set it back.
(5) DEBUG CONSOLE - USB-C to CP2102N-A02-GQFN24, CDC virtual COM port (console half of the Curiosity Nano debugger, DS50003011 3.1.2)
Divider REQUIRED (CP2102N 2.3): 22.1k/47.5k -> 3.41 V at U5 pin 8.
D_dbg pin 5 clamps raw VBUS (this node), not VBUS_DET.
D_dbg (USBLC6-2SC6) pin hookup - wire BOTH pins of each I/O pair:
pin 6 I/O1 -+- USB_DP = J_dbg D+ (A6/B6) = U5 D+ (pin 3)
pin 4 I/O2 -+- USB_DM = J_dbg D- (A7/B7) = U5 D- (pin 4)
pin 5 VBUS ---- J_dbg VBUS (A4/B9) -> R_vbus1/R_vbus2 -> VBUS_DET -> U5 VBUS (pin 8)
but the car chassis and the laptop share no DC path
1 kOhm to VIO - required in all cases
U5 runs from 3V3_SYS, NOT from VBUS. This is CP2102N Figure 2.3 (internal 5 V regulator unused, so VREGIN is
tied to VDD) plus Figure 2.6 (self-powered USB, VBUS reaching the SENSE PIN ONLY). The bus-powered Figure 2.5
ties VBUS to VREGIN instead - that is the wiring to avoid, because it would let a laptop run the bridge while
the vehicle rail is dead and drive DBG_RX into an unpowered MCU. The back-power failure mode from
bench-wiring.md is designed out rather than patched. VBUS only ever tells U5 that a host is attached.
THE CROSS IS ALREADY DONE: U5 TXD (21) drives the PIC RX (RF1) and U5 RXD (20) listens to the PIC TX (RF0),
exactly as the Nano wires CDC TX to the target UART RX (DS50003011 Figure 3-1). Do not cross it a second time.
Both directions must be populated: RF1 is how a server URL will later be written into the 1 KB Data EEPROM,
so an output-only console would foreclose it. No DTR/RTS auto-reset circuit - reset belongs to J_icsp, and an
RC on MCLR outside the sheet-3 network would fight the PICkit for the pin. Two SEPARATE 5.1 kOhm CC resistors
are required, and D+/D- must reach BOTH A6/A7 and B6/B7 for either cable orientation to work. Route the pair
at 90 Ohm differential. No series resistors on D+/D-: the CP2102N integrates the transceiver, its matching,
and the pull-ups. Programming is NOT here - the PIC18F57Q84 has no USB peripheral, so U5 is the virtual COM
port only. Program and debug are on J_icsp with a PICkit 5.
(6) STATUS LED - RF3, pin 39, active low
RF3 sinks the LED current, so the pin drives LOW to light it - which is what LATFbits.LATF3 already does in main.c.
HFINTOSC at 64 MHz. Y_hs, C_osc1, C_osc2 and Y_sosc are all quantity ZERO, which leaves OSC1 (32) and
OSC2 (33) free as general I/O. CONFIG1 MUST be programmed with RSTOSC = 000: an erased part comes up with
RSTOSC = 111, meaning "external clock", and a crystal-less board will simply never run.
(B) MCU SUPPORT component values in mcu-support-circuit.md
FARSEER CELLULAR SUPPORT CIRCUIT - Quectel BG95-M3, Mini PCIe card
Reference designators shown; component values are in cellular-support-circuit.md
Pin numbers are the 52-pin Mini PCIe edge connector (Mini PCIe Hardware Design V1.0, Table 4)
Quectel 3.2: in 2G the input peak current reaches 2.7 A, and a LOW-ESR BYPASS CAPACITOR OF NO LESS THAN 470 uF
is required to keep the rail from collapsing. C10/C11 is that reservoir; C12-C15 complete the Figure 3 ladder.
All four VCC_3V3 pins must be fed - they are spread across the connector deliberately, and feeding only one is a
current-density mistake. All fourteen GND pins (4, 9, 15, 18, 21, 26, 27, 29, 34, 35, 37, 40, 43, 50) go to plane.
Sizing arithmetic is in power-rail-notes.md. Keep buck A's inductor and switch node away from the antenna run.
(2) J2 SIGNAL MAP : every non-power pin we touch
J2 Mini PCIe socket, 52-pin full size + latch
from PIC RF4 (U3TX) through R_u3a - card RX
to PIC RF5 (U3RX) through R_u3b - card TX
from PIC RF7 (U3RTS) - Opt, flow control off by default
to PIC RF6 (U3CTS) - Opt, flow control off by default
from PIC RB0, open-drain - VIL <= 0.45 V, hold low 2-3.8 s
from PIC RB1 - Opt airplane mode, VIL <= 0.45 V
to PIC RB2 (INT2) - Opt, 120 ms low pulse on a URC
to sheet 4 - open collector, sinks up to 40 mA
to sheet 3 - 1.8 V, supplied BY the card
NO LEVEL SHIFTERS. Table 8 puts UART_RX/TX/CTS/RTS in the 3.3 V power domain and Table 10 does the same for RI,
DTR, W_DISABLE# and PERST#, so the 3.3 V PIC wires straight across. Do not fit the TXS0108 the raw-LGA guide
calls for. Only (U)SIM, PCM and I2C are 1.8 V, and none of those reach the MCU.
The UART names are CARD-RELATIVE and therefore ALREADY CROSSED: pin 11 UART_RX is "connect to DTE's TX" and pin
13 UART_TX is "connect to DTE's RX". Wire PIC TX to pin 11 and PIC RX to pin 13; do not cross them a second time.
There is NO PWRKEY on this card. Figure 1 shows an automatic power-on circuit, so the card boots whenever
3V3_CELL is live - boot order is set by buck A's EN pin (PIC RA2, high = on), not by a module key pin.
LEFT UNCONNECTED: WAKE# (1), I2C_SCL/SDA (30, 32), USIM_DET (44), PCM_CLK/DOUT/DIN/SYNC (45, 47, 49, 51), and
every RESERVED pin (3, 5, 6, 7, 16, 19, 24, 28, 33, 46, 48). Table 4 note 3: keep all reserved and unused pins
unconnected - do NOT ground them "to be safe", since several carry repurposed standard Mini PCIe functions.
(3) (U)SIM HOLDER - 1.8 V only, Quectel Figure 5 (6-pin holder)
One TVS array, <= 15 pF, covering all four SIM lines at the holder.
The card supplies USIM_VDD itself at 1.8 V; our board provides the holder and the protection network. C_sim1 must
NOT exceed 1 uF (3.3) and sits at the holder. The 33 pF caps filter EGSM900 interference; the 0 ohm links are the
Layout, all mandatory at review: holder as close to the socket as possible with trace length under 200 mm; SIM
signals kept away from RF and power-supply traces; ground between socket and holder short and wide, >= 0.5 mm;
USIM_DATA and USIM_CLK separated and shielded by surrounding ground. The holder is the only user-accessible
connector on this subsystem, so it is the realistic ESD entry point - D_sim is Req, not Rec.
(4) LED_WWAN# - network status, pin 42, open collector, active low
R_wwan IS NOT OPTIONAL if D_wwan is fitted: 3.7.4 says a resistor MUST be placed in series, and the pin will sink
up to 40 mA and cook the LED without it. 1 kOhm gives about 2 mA. Default pattern (AT+QCFG="ledmode",0): 200 ms
low / 1800 ms high = searching, 1800 / 200 = registered and idle, 125 / 125 = data transfer - readable across a paddock.
(5) USB - pins 36 / 38, optional, firmware update path
R_usb1/2 are 0 ohm and NOT MOUNTED by default (Figure 6) - they exist so the pair can be broken out to test
points. L_usb is a common-mode choke and belongs close to the socket. Route as a 90 ohm differential pair with
ground surround, never under crystals, oscillators, magnetics or RF traces, preferably on an inner layer.
(6) RF AND MECHANICAL - no host-board parts
RF: NOTHING on our board. The card carries its own 50 ohm main antenna connector and the antenna mates directly
to it - no 50 ohm trace, no matching network, no antenna feed on the host PCB. What the board must provide is
mechanical: clearance above the card for the U.FL-LP plug and its cable bend radius, a route to the enclosure
bulkhead, and strain relief. In a race car that cable sees vibration continuously - anchor it.
Mechanical: 51.0 x 30.0 mm full-size card, standard 52-pin Mini PCIe socket (e.g. Molex 679105700) WITH latch.
In a vehicle the latch is structural, not convenience; add a retaining screw or bracket. Operating range tops out
at +75 C (extended +80 C), which an enclosure near a transmission tunnel can exceed - plan the mounting spot.
(C) CELLULAR - BG95-M3 component values in cellular-support-circuit.md
FARSEER GNSS SUPPORT CIRCUIT - u-blox NEO-M9N-00B, 24-pin LCC
Reference designators shown; component values are in gnss-support-circuit.md
Sources: datasheet UBX-19014285 and integration manual UBX-19014286 (R10)
(1) U4 NEO-M9N-00B : all 24 pins, with the board action for each
50 ohm to the antenna front end - no DC block, no matching
to the bias-T, active antenna only - VCC - 0.1 V, 50 mA
external LNA enable, ACTIVE HIGH - active antenna only
to PIC RD1 (U2RX) - NMEA out, 38400 then 115200
to PIC RC2 (CCP1 capture) - 1 PPS, 30 ns RMS, 4 mA
from PIC RB3, open-drain - internal 7-13 kOhm pull-up
LEAVE OPEN = UART. Grounding it selects SPI
leave open; bring to a test point for future firmware update
Baseline rule (datasheet 5): all inputs have internal pull-ups and can be left open if unused - which is why most
of this pin list is "leave open" rather than a resistor. The two exceptions are V_USB, which must be GROUNDED, and
V_BCKP, which must be TIED TO VCC if no backup source is fitted. Neither is covered by the leave-open rule.
The LCC package has perimeter castellations at 1.1 mm pitch: joints are visible and probeable, no thermal pad, no
X-ray needed. Take the footprint and paste mask from IM Figures 37 and 38, and leave keep-out on the long edge for
de-paneling residual tabs up to 0.5 mm.
THREE CONSTRAINTS THAT ARE EASY TO VIOLATE.
1. Series resistance in the VCC line must stay UNDER 0.2 OHM (IM 4.2.1 / 4.9.1), or dynamic current generates
input voltage noise. That is a spec on FB2: choose the bead for DCR below 0.2 ohm, not just for impedance at
100 MHz. A typical 600 ohm @ 100 MHz part can easily exceed it.
2. VCC ramp rate must land between 20 and 8000 us/V, so a 0 -> 3.3 V rise takes between 66 us and 26.4 ms.
Too fast MAY PERMANENTLY DAMAGE THE DEVICE (datasheet Table 10 note 7). Buck B's ramp is checked in
power-rail-notes.md, and must be re-checked if its soft-start ever changes.
3. The VCC pad wants copper, not a thin trace: large pad, large vias down to the power layer, C_neo1 as close as
physically possible (IM 4.8.4.2). Peak draw is 100 mA during acquisition.
U4 pin 7 straight to the ground plane
V_USB MUST BE TIED TO GND when USB is unused (IM 4.2.3, repeated in the 4.3 minimal design and the 4.9.1
checklist). This is not covered by the "inputs may be left open" rule.
V_BCKP maintains the RTC and battery-backed RAM, which is the difference between a hot start of a couple of
seconds and a 24-29 s cold start every time the car is keyed off in the paddock. Backup draw is only 45 uA typ.
If no backup source is fitted, TIE V_BCKP DIRECTLY TO VCC - never leave it floating. Keep the line low-resistance:
the switchover from main to backup draws a short current peak, and a resistive path turns that into a damaging
voltage drop, so no series resistor "for isolation" here.
(4) RF FRONT END - one layout, passive or active antenna by populate / no-fit
Fit L_bias / C_bias / R_bias and omit R_bias0;
for a passive antenna do exactly the reverse.
The module has an internal DC block and internal 50 ohm matching, plus a SAW filter ahead of its LNA and an LTE
band 13 notch. DO NOT FIT A DC BLOCK OR A MATCHING NETWORK on RF_IN - they are already inside, and the SAW is what
lets an inexpensive passive antenna work next to a BG95 transmitting at ~22 dBm from a few tens of cm away.
R_bias is 22 ohm, NOT the 10 ohm in IM Table 26: supplying from VCC_RF at 3.3 V requires >= 19 ohm to hold
short-circuit current under 150 mA, and 22 ohm is the nearest standard value. A chafed coax against bodywork is
the most likely short in a race car, and this resistor is what stops it destroying the bias-T or the internal feed.
D_rf is REQUIRED (IM 4.5.2): an external RF connector is a conduction path for destructive signals. RF_IN routes
as a grounded co-planar waveguide referenced to layer 2, matched to 50 ohm, via-shielded along its entire length,
with vias around the RF_IN pad and NO STUBS. Absolute limits: 0 dBm in band, +13 dBm out of band, 30 dB max
external gain - do not stack an active antenna with a further LNA.
(5) UART AND CONTROL TO THE PIC - direct, no level shifting, no series resistors
Both ends sit on 3V3_SYS, so the levels are comfortable in both directions: the NEO needs Vih >= 0.8 x VCC =
2.64 V and swings to within 0.4 V of the rails at 2 mA, and the PIC is on the same rail. Max 5 mA per digital
I/O, and NO HARDWARE FLOW CONTROL is supported. TIMEPULSE is worth routing even though the firmware does not use
it yet - 30 ns RMS in hardware capture beats UART arrival time by orders of magnitude for correlating position
(D) GNSS - NEO-M9N component values in gnss-support-circuit.md
